page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-256 is a memory-dense compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is delivered via an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 16 dedicated physical cores supporting two threads per core, providing a total of 32 vCPUs. Paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, the environment provides 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, matching the characteristics of a memory-optimized footprint.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this configuration, and no local disk storage is bundled with the instance. All persistent storage operations rely on external network-attached volumes. For network connectivity, the server configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation allows high-memory operations without requiring the provisioning of excessive compute cores. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-256 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise backend platforms, and extract-transform-load data pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance driven by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory. This sizing establishes an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, positioning the instance for memory-intensive footprints. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, operates without hardware GPUs, and provides no integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystems. By supplying dedicated CPU cores paired with large memory density, the instance balances cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial working memory without necessitating disproportionate CPU thread counts. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.16-256 is well matched for memory-resident caching systems, medium-to-large relational databases, enterprise resource planning backends, and data transformation pipelines.
